summary: Iranian Revolutionary Guard general Qassem Soleimani rose from a poor Kerman childhood to run the Quds Force, building proxy militias across Iraq, Syria, Lebanon and beyond until a US strike killed him in Baghdad in 2020.

evidence.note: Birth in 1957 in a village in Kerman Province; father's debt to the Shah's government
Sent with Revolutionary Guard to crush the Kurdish uprising at Mahabad at age 23
Reagan administration armed both Iran and Iraq; intelligence aided chemical attacks
After 1988 posted to eastern frontier to fight opium smugglers and the Taliban
Appointed head of the Quds Force; its role in asymmetric warfare explained
1998 Mazar-i-Sharif crisis; backs Northern Alliance instead of invading Afghanistan
2002 Axis of Evil speech ends US-Iran cooperation in Kabul
Quds Force supplies EFPs to Iraqi insurgents and lets jihadists transit Syria
Directs Shia militias propping up Assad in the Syrian civil war
Leaked Iranian cables on militia abuses against Sunnis and his self-promotion
State-built cult of personality and martyrdom image, Instagram following
Killed by US missile strike leaving Baghdad airport, January 2020

notes: Recorded days after the assassination with live news breaks, but the bulk is a life story, so deep-dive rather than current-affairs. Primary theme follows the taxonomy's own Soleimani example; war-war-crimes is a close alternative. No content warning: chemical attacks, the Mazar massacre and Assad's prisons are mentioned briefly, not in detail.
